Write the specification workbook from a spec, without a plan

Source: R/tteplan_excel_spec_summary.R
tteplan_excel_spec_summary.Rd

Writes the Study Specification sheet and the Target trial protocol sheet from the spec file and a code registry. The function reads no skeleton, rawbatch or registry data file, so it runs before s0.

Usage

tteplan_excel_spec_summary(
  spec_path,
  path,
  code_registry = NULL,
  period_width = 4L,
  global_max_isoyearweek = NULL,
  protocol_ett_id = NULL
)

Arguments

spec_path

Character(1), the path of the spec YAML. The function reads it with tteplan_read_spec().

path

Character(1), the output .xlsx path. The function overwrites an existing file.

code_registry

The code registry that resolves each variable to its codes. One of these:

  • NULL. Every variable is written as unresolved, as for a plan that has no code registry.

  • A RegistryStudy. The function uses $summary_table() and reads no data.

  • A data.table with the columns of RegistryStudy$summary_table(): name, codes, label and generated_columns.

period_width

Integer, the width in weeks of the enrollment period. It has the default of tteplan_from_spec_and_registrystudy(). The Target trial protocol sheet states it.

global_max_isoyearweek

Character(1) or NULL, the administrative censoring boundary as an isoyearweek, for example "2023-52". NULL writes not built (spec only) in the Admin censoring: row.

protocol_ett_id

Character(1) or NULL, the ETT that the Target trial protocol sheet documents. NULL takes the first ETT of the grid. An id that the grid does not hold gives a warning, and the sheet then documents the first ETT.

Value

path, invisibly.

Details

Each cell holds the value that TTEPlan$excel_spec_summary() writes for a plan at s0 from the same spec, code registry, period_width and protocol_ett_id. The one exception is the Admin censoring: row. s0 reads that value from the first skeleton unless you supply it. Here the row reads not built (spec only) unless you supply global_max_isoyearweek.

Only s1 decides the rare-condition rule. The workbook therefore states the rule as not decided yet, and it has no Sparse conditions sheet. The function builds the ETT grid with the code of tteplan_from_spec_and_registrystudy(), so the protocol sheet documents the same ETT for the same protocol_ett_id.

See also

tteplan_from_spec_and_registrystudy(), TTEPlan

Other tte_spec: tteplan_apply_derived_confounders(), tteplan_apply_exclusions(), tteplan_from_spec_and_registrystudy(), tteplan_read_spec(), tteplan_validate_spec()

Examples

spec_dir <- tempfile()
dir.create(spec_dir)
spec_path <- file.path(spec_dir, "spec_v001.yaml")
writeLines(
  c(
    "study:",
    "  title: Example study",
    "  principal_investigator: Example PI",
    "  implementation:",
    "    project_prefix: example",
    "    version: v001",
    "inclusion_criteria:",
    "  isoyears: [2010, 2020]",
    "exclusion_criteria:",
    "  - name: Prior oophorectomy",
    "    implementation:",
    "      source_variable: os_oophorectomy",
    "      window: lifetime_before_baseline",
    "confounders:",
    "  - name: Age",
    "    implementation:",
    "      variable: rd_age_continuous",
    "outcomes:",
    "  - name: Outcome",
    "    implementation:",
    "      variable: osd_outcome",
    "follow_up:",
    "  - {label: 1 year, weeks: 52}",
    "enrollments:",
    "  - id: '01'",
    "    name: A vs B",
    "    observed_var: {sentinel: row_presence}",
    "    intervention_tolerance_weeks: 0",
    "    comparator_tolerance_weeks: 0",
    "    additional_inclusion:",
    "      - {name: Age 50-59, type: age_range, min: 50, max: 59}",
    "    treatment:",
    "      arms: {intervention: A, comparator: B}",
    "      implementation:",
    "        variable: rd_tx",
    "        intervention_value: a",
    "        comparator_value: b",
    "        comparator_to_intervention_ratio: 2",
    "        seed: 1"
  ),
  spec_path
)
study <- RegistryStudy$new(data_rawbatch_dir = spec_dir)
study$register_codes(
  codes = list(oophorectomy = c("LAE20", "LAE21", "LAF10")),
  fn = swereg::add_operations,
  groups = list(os = c("inpatient", "outpatient"))
)
out <- tteplan_excel_spec_summary(
  spec_path = spec_path,
  path = file.path(spec_dir, "spec_v001.xlsx"),
  code_registry = study
)
#> Spec summary saved to: /tmp/RtmpGMWLua/file1dd14174d18b/spec_v001.xlsx
openxlsx::getSheetNames(out)
#> [1] "Study Specification"   "Target trial protocol"
unlink(spec_dir, recursive = TRUE)
